{{Short description|Anglo-Canadian mathematician}}
'''Stephen William Drury''' is an Anglo-Canadian [[mathematician]] and [[professor]] of mathematics at [[McGill University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mcgill.ca/mathstat/stephen-w-drury|title=Stephen W Drury|website=McGill University|language=en|access-date=2019-02-11}}</ref> He specializes in [[Mathematical Analysis|mathematical analysis]], [[harmonic analysis]] and [[Linear Algebra|linear algebra]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.mcgill.ca/drury/research/research.php|title=S. W. Drury – Research Interests|website=|access-date=2019-02-11}}</ref>  He received his doctorate from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1970 under the supervision of [[Nicholas Varopoulos]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=66412&fChrono=1|title=Sam (Stephen William) Drury|website=Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> and completed his postdoctoral training at the [[University of Paris-Sud|Faculté des sciences d'Orsay]], France. He was recruited to McGill by Professor [[Carl S. Herz|Carl Herz]] in 1972.

Among other contributions, he solved the [[Sidon set]] union problem,<ref>Drury, S.W., 1970, Sur les ensembles de Sidon, ''C.R. Acad. Sci. Paris,'' 271, pp. 162–164</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/199607/comm-herz.pdf|title=Carl Herz 1930–1995|website=American Mathematical Society|access-date=29 July 2019}}</ref> worked on restrictions of [[Fourier transform|Fourier]] and [[Radon transform|Radon]] transforms to curves,<ref>Drury, S.W., 1985. Restriction of Fourier transforms to curves. ''Ann. Inst. Fourier'', ''35''(1), pp. 117–123.</ref> and generalized [[von Neumann's inequality]].<ref>Drury, S.W., 1978. A generalization of von Neumann’s inequality to the complex ball. ''Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society'', ''68''(3), pp. 300–304.</ref> In [[operator theory]], the Drury–Arveson space is named after [[William Arveson]] and him.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cms-math.net.technion.ac.il/files/2016/04/Quanlei_Fang_mvot2017-1.pdf|title=Operator theory in Drury–Arveson Space|last=Fang|first=Quanlei|date=June 2017|website=Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|access-date=29 July 2019}}</ref>

His research now pertains to the interplay between [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] theory and harmonic analysis and their applications to [[graph theory]].
